teams.heading: Fiji drop to twelfth in international standings after three consecutive defeats
teams.body: Fiji currently occupy 12th place in the international table after failing to secure a victory in their opening three matches. Across these fixtures, the side has conceded 145 points. They have scored 49 points over the same period, leaving them with a points difference of minus 96. This run follows their last outing, which ended in a 17-33 defeat against Scotland in the third round. Despite this sequence, they hope to return to the heights of 2023, when they achieved their highest ever world ranking of No. 7.

teams.heading: Richard Wigglesworth warns Courtney Lawes and Joe Marchant over England recalls
teams.body: England assistant coach Richard Wigglesworth has warned returning veterans Courtney Lawes and Joe Marchant that they must perform "over and above" their Premiership rivals to earn autumn recalls. Despite returning to England with Sale after spells in France, neither player was named in Steve Borthwick's 36-man training squad this week. Wigglesworth confirmed the door remains open, but stressed the duo must outshine incumbent squad members during the opening weeks of the domestic season to force their way back into Borthwick's plans.

teams.heading: Argentina XV announce November tour clash against England 'A' at Bath
teams.body: The Argentina XV will travel to face England 'A' for the first time in nearly two decades at Bath's Recreation Ground this November. The uncapped fixture, confirmed by organisers, will run in parallel with the senior national side's Nations Championship test against Ireland in Dublin. teams.heading: Carter Gordon fractures leg during Argentina draw to disrupt Wallabies' backline
teams.body: The Wallabies' playmaking depth faces a severe test after first-choice fly-half Carter Gordon suffered a leg fracture during Sunday's 28-28 draw with Argentina in Mendoza. Scans confirmed the 25-year-old will miss around two months, ruling him out of the upcoming clash against South Africa and the Bledisloe Cup. Head coach Les Kiss must now choose between Ben Donaldson, who struggled to impress in Mendoza, and the fit-again Tom Lynagh, who is scheduled to return from a lengthy injury lay-off in Super Rugby AU this Saturday.

teams.heading: Timothy Lafaele and fellow Japan stars settle League One eligibility court battle
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has revised its controversial player registration rules after reaching a court settlement with a group of 25 players. The legal challenge, spearheaded by high-profile Brave Blossoms internationals including Timothy Lafaele and Jiwon Gu, opposed a planned domestic split. Under the new agreement reached at the Tokyo District Court, the league introduced special measures, ensuring that any veteran with 30 or more test caps will be reclassified under the premier category.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie loses captain Ardie Savea as injuries force Baltimore rotation
teams.body: Dave Rennie must name a new captain for Saturday’s series finale in Baltimore after Ardie Savea was ruled out with a shoulder injury. The All Blacks arrived in the United States following a gruelling journey from Johannesburg, with Luke Jacobson and Quinn Tupaea also sidelined following the third test. Rennie confirmed he will "share the load" to bring in players with fresh energy. Richie Mo’unga is under consideration to replace Ruben Love at fly-half, while Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord could return from concussion.

teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has handed Morné van den Berg a start for Saturday’s series finale against New Zealand in Baltimore. The Lions scrum-half replaces Cobus Reinach, who drops to the bench, in one of only two changes to the starting line-up. Damian Willemse also returns to the XV to replace the injured Cheslin Kolbe. Erasmus explained that Van den Berg "deserves a start" following a strong cameo during the victory in Soweto as South Africa target a series victory on neutral ground.
